    "Ancient humans engaged in cannibalism and made bowls from human skulls, according to a study of bones discovered in Gough's Cave in Somerset. Teeth marks on the bones suggest that the corpses were eaten by other humans. Researchers used modern radiocarbon techniques to date the deposits in the cave, which were determined to be 14,700 years old. The skulls had been stripped of flesh and shaped into bowls for use, and the practice may have been a traditional way of disposing of the dead. Scientists believe the humans may have been Cro-Magnon hunter-gatherers called Magdalenians.": 1

    "Doctors at University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust have successfully developed a single procedure that can diagnose cancer of the lungs within 30 minutes, helping to save thousands of lives every year. The endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) involves inserting a tiny camera down a patient's throat and taking a tissue sample in one go, allowing doctors to instantly assess the type and severity of the cancer. The method halves the time it takes between a patient's first hospital appointment and the start of their treatment, while EBUS patients survive for an average of 503 days after diagnosis - significantly longer than those who undergo traditional techniques. With more than 40,000 people diagnosed with lung cancer in the UK each year, the approach is expected to be rolled out across the NHS in the near future.": 1

Although genocide was not a defined crime at the time, this was the first genocide of the 20th century. Victims died in mass burnings, drownings, torture, gas, poison, disease, and starvation.
